verb.the5VerbForms: The 5 verb forms, spelling rules, how to pronounce -ed/-s, and every tense in a table – including the passive.
verb.modalVerbsDoNot: Modal verbs do not change with the subject (he can, never “cans”), have no to-infinitive or -ing form, and are always followed by the bare infinitive without “to”.
verb.question: Question
verb.notInOurList: Not in our list – conjugated by the regular rules
verb.ukBritishUsageUs: UK = British usage, US = American usage. The tables below follow the variety you choose.
verb.irregularVerbLearnV2: Irregular verb: learn V2 and V3 by heart. The -ing and -s forms still follow the normal rules.
verb.justAddEdIng: Just add -ed, -ing or -s – no spelling change.
verb.subject: Subject
verb.almostNeverUsedIn: Almost never used in real English.
verb.thePassiveIsRare: The passive is rare in this tense – use another tense instead.
verb.stativeVerbUsuallyNot: Stative verb: usually not used in continuous tenses (I know, not I am knowing).
verb.continuousFormsAreFine: Continuous forms are fine for an action meaning (I’m thinking about it), but not for an opinion or state (I think so).
verb.theNegativeOfMust: The negative of “must have” (deduction) is can’t have / couldn’t have; it is rarely used in questions.
verb.actionsHappeningNowOrNear: Actions happening now, or near-future arrangements.
verb.experiencesPresentResultsAndThings: Experiences, present results, and things that have just happened.
verb.actionsContinuingFromThePast: Actions continuing from the past until now, focusing on the process.
verb.finishedActionsAtASpecific: Finished actions at a specific time in the past.
verb.actionsInProgressAtA: Actions in progress at a moment in the past.
verb.anActionThatHappenedBefore: An action that happened before another past action.
verb.aProcessThatContinuedUp: A process that continued up to a point in the past.
verb.existingPlansAndPredictionsBased: Existing plans and predictions based on evidence.
verb.actionsInProgressAtAMoment: Actions in progress at a moment in the future.
verb.actionsThatWillBeFinished: Actions that will be finished before a point in the future.
verb.aProcessThatWillContinue: A process that will continue up to a point in the future.
verb.theFutureSeenFromThe: The future seen from the past (reported speech).
verb.aPastPlanThatOften: A past plan (that often did not happen).
verb.regretOrCriticismTheRight: Regret or criticism: the right thing was not done.
verb.aPastPossibilityThatDid: A past possibility that did not happen.
verb.anUncertainGuessAboutThe: An uncertain guess about the past.
verb.aPossibleGuessAboutThe: A possible guess about the past.
verb.anAlmostCertainConclusionAbout: An almost certain conclusion about the past.
verb.ifAVerbEndsIn: If a verb ends in consonant + vowel + consonant and the last syllable is stressed, double the final consonant (stop → stopped, begin → beginning).
verb.britishEnglishDoublesTheFinal: British English doubles the final -l (travelled); American English does not (traveled).
verb.consonantYChangeYTo: Consonant + y: change y to i, then add -ed/-es (studied, studies). Vowel + y keeps the y (played).
verb.dropTheSilentEBefore: Drop the silent -e before -ing, and add only -d for -ed (making, loved).
verb.verbsEndingInEeOe: Verbs ending in -ee, -oe or -ye keep the -e before -ing (agreeing, canoeing).
verb.addKAfterIcBefore: Add k after -ic before -ed/-ing to keep the /k/ sound (panicked, panicking).
verb.addEsAfterSX: Add -es after s, x, z, ch, sh and consonant + o (watches, goes).
verb.theFinalSoundIsT: The final sound is /t/ or /d/ → add an extra syllable /ɪd/.
verb.theFinalSoundIsVoiceless: The final sound is voiceless (/p k f s ʃ tʃ θ/) → say /t/.
verb.theFinalSoundIsA: The final sound is a vowel or voiced (/b g v z m n l r/…) → say /d/.
verb.afterAHissingSoundS: After a hissing sound /s z ʃ ʒ tʃ dʒ/ → add an extra syllable /ɪz/.
verb.afterAVoicelessSoundP: After a voiceless sound /p t k f θ/ → say /s/.
verb.afterAVowelOrVoiced: After a vowel or voiced sound → say /z/.
verb.afterDidDidnTUse: After did / didn’t, use the base form.
verb.afterHaveHasHadUse: After have / has / had, use the past participle (V3), not V2.
verb.afterDoesDoesnTThe: After does / doesn’t, the verb takes no -s.
verb.stativeVerbsAreUsuallyNot: Stative verbs are usually not used in continuous tenses.
verb.spellingMistakeSeeTheSpelling: Spelling mistake – see the spelling rules above.
verb.agreeIsAVerbDo: “agree” is a verb – do not use it with am/is/are.
verb.thisVerbIsFollowedBy: This verb is followed by -ing, not by to + verb.
verb.arriveInACityOr: arrive in (a city or country) / arrive at (a place) – never “arrive to”.
verb.lieRestFlatLayLain: lie (rest flat) – lay – lain has no object; lay (put down) – laid – laid needs an object.
verb.riseGoUpByItself: rise (go up by itself) has no object; raise (lift or increase something) needs an object.
verb.beBornIsAFixed: “be born” is a fixed form: I was born.
verb.beActsAsItsOwn: “be” acts as its own auxiliary – it never uses do / does / did.
verb.lookForwardToIngTo: look forward to + -ing (“to” is a preposition here).
verb.suggestRecommendThatSubjectVerb: suggest / recommend + that + subject + verb (or + -ing), not “someone to + verb”.
verb.neverUseTwoModalVerbs: Never use two modal verbs together: say “will be able to”.
verb.lendGiveForATime: lend = give for a time; borrow = take for a time.
verb.tellAPersonSaySomething: tell + a person; say + something (say to someone).
verb.britishEnglishUsesHaveGot: British English uses “have got”; “gotten” is American English.
verb.afterAModalVerbUse: After a modal verb, use the base form with no -s.
verb.modalVerbsMoveToThe: Modal verbs move to the front in questions – no “do”.
usage.beforeTheSubjectOften: Before the subject, often followed by a comma.
usage.beforeMainVerbsAfter: Before main verbs; after be and auxiliaries.
usage.afterTheVerbAnd: After the verb and its object.
usage.couldnTSavePlease: Couldn’t save – please try again later
usage.typeAWordE: Type a word, e.g. interested, depend, stop
usage.findHowAWord: Find how a word is used
usage.dependentPrepositionsVerbPatterns: Dependent prepositions, verb patterns, adverb position, sentence structures and confusing words – with examples, common mistakes and quick practice.
usage.adjectivesVerbsAndNouns: Adjectives, verbs and nouns + prepositions: interested in, depend on, reason for…
usage.enjoyDoingDecideTo: enjoy doing, decide to do, stop/remember/try change meaning, make sb do…
usage.hardHardlyLateLately: hard/hardly, late/lately, where always goes, how to spell -ly
usage.itIsAdjTo: It is + adj + to-V, too/enough, so/such…that, despite/although…
usage.learnWholeChunksNot: Learn whole chunks, not single words: “interested in”, not just “interested”.
usage.readTheExamplesAloud: Read the examples aloud – your ears remember prepositions better than your eyes.
usage.savePhrasesToYour: Save phrases to your words so you review them right before you forget.
usage.doTheQuickPractice: Do the quick practice at the end of each page to check yourself right away.
usage.donTPutAn: Don’t put an adverb between a verb and its object: “speak English well”, not “speak well English”.
usage.chooseTheCorrectAnswer: Choose the correct answer – you’ll see the result instantly. Shortcuts: A–D or 1–4.
usage.veryGoodTakeAnother: Very good! Take another look at the one you missed.
usage.readTheExamplesAbove: Read the examples above again, then try once more.
usage.otherPartsOfSpeech: Other parts of speech – tap to see usage or look up the meaning.
usage.changeThePrepositionAnd: Change the preposition and the meaning changes – learn the whole phrase.
usage.whatFollowsThisVerb: What follows this verb: to-V, V-ing, an object…?
usage.mistakesLearnersOftenMake: Mistakes learners often make – especially when translating word for word.
usage.thereAreNoUsage: There are no usage notes for “{w}” yet. Here is what Lexkite knows about this word, plus similar words.
